summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a renewable fuel content scheme for motor vehicle fuel supplied in Australia, supported by an administrator, reporting requirements and enforceable supply rules.
Regulations would require renewable fuel content of at least 5 per cent from 1 July 2017 and 10 per cent from 1 July 2020.
The main scheme would begin on proclamation, with exceptions for emergency-law supplies and fuel reasonably expected to undergo further processing to meet the regulations.
changes: Refineries, blenders and importers could earn transferable credits for renewable content above required levels.
Suppliers dealing with parties other than end users would have to provide compliance documentation.
Covered suppliers would have to retain records of fuel supplied.
Producers and importers would have to submit annual statements in the administrator’s required form.
summary.affected: Fuel producers, processors, refineries, blenders, importers, covered suppliers and the Renewable Fuel Program Administrator are affected.
